original_record.subject: chemistry
original_record.question: Which of the following statement is true of a proton?

options.A: The mass of a proton is 1.0008 g
options.B: The mass of a proton is
options.C: The mass of proton is 1840 times the mass of an electron
options.D: The total mass of the proton in a particular nucleus is always half the nucleus is always half the nuclear mass.

original_record.ai_explanation: The mass of a proton is approximately 1840 times the mass of an electron, which is the correct statement among the options given.

candidate.subject: chemistry
candidate.question: Which statement about a proton is correct?

options.B: Its mass is one-twelfth the molar mass of carbon
options.C: Its mass is approximately 1840 times the mass of an electron
options.D: The total mass of the protons in any nucleus is always half its nuclear mass

candidate.ai_explanation: A proton is about 1836 times as massive as an electron, often rounded to 1840 in school calculations. Its mass is about 1.67 × 10⁻²⁴ g. A molar mass describes one mole, not one particle, and nuclei do not all have equal numbers of protons and neutrons.
